strings.title: Confession on Air
strings.hint: Compare the late-night caller's voice with today's victim… then ask the forbidden question: who closed yesterday's case in such a hurry? And whose pistol was it?
strings.solvedText:
The culprit: retired investigator Salah Berro, the celebrated investigator of the old case itself.

Twenty years earlier, he fabricated the River Mill case to close it quickly and advance his career. He concealed testimony that cleared the accused and pressured the only witness, Fathi Murad, into silence. When Fathi called the radio station to confess what he had hidden, mentioning details never published, Salah immediately recognized his voice. He knew the new testimony would reopen the file and bury him instead. He silenced Fathi with a bullet from his old service pistol, officially "missing" since his retirement.

The caller's voiceprint matching the victim, forged signatures in the old file, and a bullet matching a pistol supposedly lost from his own custody proved his guilt.
strings.summary.text: During the radio program "An Evening of Memories," an elderly man called in with a trembling voice and confessed on air: "The River Mill case twenty years ago… the man imprisoned for it is innocent. I was a witness who stayed silent." He gave details never printed in any newspaper, then hung up. Forty-eight hours later, Fathi Murad, the mill's former guard, was found shot dead in the chest. Who silenced the witness before he could complete his confession, and why after twenty years?

strings.summary.victim.note: A double case: today's murder reopens yesterday's injustice

strings.scene.address: The victim's house — the edge of the old town, near the mill
strings.scene.intro: One expertly fired shot from the doorway: the killer neither entered nor disturbed anything. An execution, not a robbery. On the victim's table lay an open notebook, with trembling handwriting: "I'll tell it all on Thursday on the radio, naming names this time."
strings.scene.photos[0].cap: The studio that received the first confession
strings.scene.photos[1].cap: Fathi Murad's house — the kitchen threshold
strings.scene.notes[0]: A single shot from the doorway — a trained hand
strings.scene.notes[1]: The victim's notebook: a full confession "naming names" planned for Thursday
strings.scene.notes[2]: No theft or disturbance — simply silencing a witness
strings.scene.notes[3]: The details in the radio call had never appeared in the newspapers
strings.evidence[0].title: Radio Confession Recording
strings.evidence[0].desc: The caller's voiceprint matches victim Fathi Murad by 97%. The man who confessed is the dead man.
strings.evidence[1].title: The Bullet
strings.evidence[1].desc: Matches an old service pistol listed as "missing" in investigator Salah Berro's retirement record.
strings.evidence[2].title: River Mill File
strings.evidence[2].desc: Hidden testimony clears the convicted man. Examination shows that signatures on the records were written by one hand in a single sitting.
strings.evidence[3].title: The Victim's Notebook
strings.evidence[3].desc: "Naming names this time." The killer knew the next confession would be more dangerous than the first.
strings.evidence[4].title: An Old Threatening Letter
strings.evidence[4].desc: A yellowed sheet from twenty years ago: "Mills grind witnesses before wheat." The handwriting will be compared.
strings.evidence[5].title: Prison Visit Log
strings.evidence[5].desc: The man convicted in the old case was released two months ago. The mill victim's brother visited him twice before his release.
strings.suspects[0].name: Ezzat Nimr, the Former Convict
strings.suspects[0].alibi: "I was at the rehabilitation center, wearing an electronic tag that records every step."
strings.suspects[0].statement: For twenty years I shouted that I was innocent and nobody listened… then the man confesses on the radio and is killed? Whoever killed him killed the proof of my innocence too. My electronic tag is more truthful than all of you. Check it.
strings.suspects[1].name: Salah Berro
strings.suspects[1].job: Retired investigator — the hero of the old case
strings.suspects[1].alibi: "I'm retired and keep birds. I was alone that night, as old men usually are."
strings.suspects[1].statement: I closed the mill case honorably with the evidence available at the time. History cannot be judged retroactively. My missing pistol? It vanished during the equipment handover ten years ago, and there is a report. I suggest you look at the recently released prisoner. Aged anger is the most dangerous kind.
strings.suspects[2].name: Samir, the Original Victim's Brother
strings.suspects[2].relation: Brother of the original mill murder victim
strings.suspects[2].alibi: "I was far away at the weekly livestock market. The sales are recorded under people's names."
strings.suspects[2].statement: For twenty years I believed my brother's killer had been imprisoned… then the confession said the truth had been buried twice. I visited Ezzat in prison to hear his account for myself and left doubting everyone. If I killed anyone, it would be the forger… but I want a trial for my brother, not another body.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Radio Presenter
strings.witnesses[0].statement: Before hanging up, he said: "The man who threatened me back then is still alive and wears a gold watch on his left wrist." We were afraid to broadcast that sentence. The retired investigator who visited the next morning "to inquire" was wearing one.
strings.witnesses[1].name: The Victim's Neighbor
strings.witnesses[1].role: Witness on the night of the murder
strings.witnesses[1].statement: An old gray car parked some distance from the house. A heavy-footed man got out and knew the way without looking around. Older people who know a place walk like that.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Widow of a Former Colleague
strings.witnesses[2].statement: Before he died, my husband, may he rest in peace, used to say: "The mill file is a disgrace to us. Salah closed it with a ruler and an eraser." We were afraid then… everyone was afraid of Salah.
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Witness Murder Report
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body: The victim's neighbor reported the incident after noticing the door ajar. Death had occurred the previous night.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Bullet Report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body: A 9 mm bullet with distinctive barrel markings matches a batch of old service pistols, including the pistol "missing" from Berro's custody.
strings.folders[1].docs[1].title: Voiceprint Report
strings.folders[1].docs[1].body: A 97% match between the radio caller and the victim, using family recordings for comparison.
strings.folders[2].name: Interviews
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Ezzat Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body: His electronic tag places him at the rehabilitation center all night. He is physically ruled out.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Berro Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body: Confident and condescending. His sole mistake was describing the body as being "at the kitchen threshold," a detail neither published nor mentioned in his presence.
strings.folders[2].docs[2].title: Samir Interview
strings.folders[2].docs[2].body: The livestock market places him far away. He voluntarily handed over notes from his prison visits.
strings.folders[3].name: Records
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Mill File Audit
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body: Exonerating testimony was omitted from the final record. The signatures of three "procedural witnesses" were written by a single hand, that of the file's author.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Old Equipment Custody Record
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body: The pistol's "loss" was documented in a record Berro signed for himself as both the person handing it over and the recipient, a loophole ten years old.
strings.folders[4].name: Confidential files
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: The Gold Watch Sentence
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: The unbroadcast portion of the call and the presenter's testimony: the person who heard the description and the man it described met in the radio station lobby the next morning. His inquiry was really reconnaissance about a threat.
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Record Reopening the Mill Case
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body: By order of the prosecution: reopen the old file, suspend the effects of Ezzat Nimr's conviction pending exoneration, and combine the two files as one crime spanning twenty years.
strings.reports[0].title: The Continuing Crime Report
strings.reports[0].author: Investigation team
strings.reports[0].body: Today's killing protected yesterday's forgery. The only person who stood to lose from the full confession was the author of the original file. The second true victim: twenty years of an innocent man's life.
strings.reports[1].title: Slip of the Tongue Report
strings.reports[1].author: Assigned investigator
strings.reports[1].body: "The kitchen threshold": three words spoken by a man who had never officially visited the scene. Experience makes killers more precise… and their confidence exposes them.
strings.notes[0].text: The man who confessed is the victim. Who feared his confession?
strings.notes[1].text: Who described a scene he had never entered?
